🧾 Ingredients
🥟 Meat Pie Layer
Minced beef (or chicken)
1 small onion (chopped)
1 tsp curry powder
1 tsp thyme
Salt + pepper
1 tbsp oil
1 tbsp flour (to thicken)
🍫 Chocolate Sugar Layer
1 cup melted chocolate
2–3 tbsp sugar (or condensed milk for extra madness)
Crushed biscuits or cookies (optional crunch)
🍕 Pizza Base
Pizza dough (store-bought or homemade)
1 tbsp butter or olive oil
🧀 Optional Chaos Toppings
Mozzarella cheese (for salty balance)
Marshmallows (if you want full “MrBeast energy”)
Drizzle honey or caramel
👨‍🍳 How to Make It
1. 🥩 Make the Meat Pie Filling
Heat oil in a pan
Add onions → cook till soft
Add minced meat
Season with curry, thyme, salt, pepper
Stir until cooked
Add flour + tiny water to make it slightly thick and juicy (not dry)
2. 🍕 Prepare the Pizza Base
Roll out dough into a large circle
Lightly brush with butter or olive oil
Pre-bake for 5 minutes at 180°C (so it doesn’t go soggy)
3. 🍫 Make the Sweet Layer
Melt chocolate
Mix in sugar (or condensed milk)
Optional: crush biscuits into it for crunch
4. 🧱 Build the Beast Pizza

Layer in this order:

Pizza base
Meat pie filling (spread evenly)
Light sprinkle of cheese (optional but recommended)
Drizzle chocolate sugar sauce all over
Add marshmallows or cookie crumbs on top
5. 🔥 Bake
Bake at 180°C for 10–12 minutes
Stop when chocolate is slightly gooey and cheese is melted
6. 🎉 Finish Like MrBeast
Drizzle honey or caramel on top
Slice into huge “challenge pieces”
Serve dramatically like:
“Whoever eats this in 60 seconds wins $10,000…” (don’t actually do that 💀)
🍽️ Taste Profile
First bite: sweet chocolate explosion 🍫
Second: savory meat pie kick 🥩
Third: confusion… then addiction 😭
⚠️ Real Talk

This is not normal pizza. It’s a:

it was really awesome. I will never forget that.

comment_text: because both the station and the astronauts inside are in a continuous state of freefall around the Earth Gravity at the altitude of the ISS is about 90% as strong as it is on the ground.The ISS travels sideways at an incredible speed of over 17,500 mph (28,000 km/h)Because the station moves sideways so fast, the Earth curves away at the exact same rate that the station falls toward it Since the ISS, the astronauts, and all the objects inside fall at the exact same rate, there is no physical support force (like a floor pushing up against your feet). This lack of contact force makes them feel and appear weightless, or in microgravity. Because of this high forward speed, as the station is pulled downward by gravity, it continuously misses the Earth as the planet curves beneath it

comment_text:
Bhel Puri 🥜🍅🍿
.
Ingredients:
	•	1 medium onion (finely chopped)
	•	1 medium tomato (finely chopped)
	•	1-2 green chillies (finely chopped)
	•	A handful of crushed Lays chips (any flavor you like)
	•	A handful of Kurkure (any flavor)
	•	A handful of namkeens (like Haldiram’s bhujia/sev/farsan)
	•	A few roasted peanuts
	•	½ tsp chaat masala (or to taste)
	•	Juice of ½ lemon (or to taste)
	•	Fresh coriander leaves (optional, chopped)
.
Instructions:
	1.	In a large bowl, add chopped onion, tomato, and green chillies.
	2.	Squeeze lemon juice and add chaat masala. Mix well.
	3.	Now add crushed Lays, Kurkure, namkeen, and peanuts.
	4.	Mix everything just before serving to keep it crunchy.
	5.	Taste and adjust lemon/chaat masala if needed.
	6.	Garnish with coriander (optional) and serve immediately.

Don’t be surprised if these fish die within a few days. If you want your fish to survive and stay healthy, keep these points in mind:

	4.	Give your tank time to cycle and allow beneficial bacteria to establish. This helps keep the water safe, as uncycled tanks often lead to deadly ammonia spikes — a very common beginner mistake.

And above all, remember — they’re living beings, not decorations.
Happy fishkeeping!

Ye video pe bahut jada views he aur log ise dekh kar same galti karenge aur fish ek hafte bhi nhi rahegi. 
1. Kabhi bhi detergent ya chemical se aquarium, substrate/rock, showpiece saaf nhi karna. Sirf normal pani use karna 
2. New aquarium ke ek hafte baad fish kharidna
3. New aquarium me pani bhar dena aur filter laga dena, thoda sa fish food daal dena aur filter ko continuous chalu rakhna. Pata he aap sochenge fish to daali nhi khana kyu daala, isse aquarium cycle hota he, good bacteria produce hote he
4. Ek hafte baad fish kharidna aur direct nhi daalna, vo panni ko pani me terne dena 30min tak taki panni ke pani ka temperature aur aquarium ke pani ka temperature aame ho jaye. 
5. Fir fish ko aquarium me daalna, panni ka pani fek dena
6. Bahot hi kam fish aquarium me daalna nhi samajta to chatgpt ko puchna mere pass itna bada aquarium he me konsi fish kitni daalu
7. Har hafte 30% pani change karna aur filter dhona sirf pani se no (chemical/detergent)
8. Tum sochonge ki aquarium clean clear nhi dikh raha to me 100% pani change karunga to soch lena fish nhi bachegi(isse good bacteria khatam ho jate he)
9. Me 2010 se fish hobby me hu bahot galti ki he bas tum isko follow karoge to fish Happy rahegi

Gravy Momos 🌶️🥟
.
Ingredients:
	•	8–10 steamed momos 
	•	1 medium onion (sliced)
	•	½ capsicum (sliced)
	•	1 tsp oregano
	•	½ tsp chilli flakes
	•	1 tbsp Schezwan sauce
	•	1 tbsp mayonnaise
	•	1 tbsp tomato ketchup
	•	½ cup water (for gravy consistency)
	•	1 tbsp oil
	•	Salt to taste
	•	Fresh coriander (chopped)

Method:
	1.	Prepare Momos
	•	Take steamed momos and deep fry them until golden and crispy. Keep aside.
	2.	Make the Gravy Base
	•	Heat oil in a pan.
	•	Sauté onions and capsicum on high flame for 1–2 minutes until slightly crunchy.
	3.	Add Flavors
	•	Add oregano, chilli flakes, Schezwan sauce, mayonnaise, and tomato ketchup.
	•	Mix well until sauces combine.
	4.	Make Gravy
	•	Add about ½ cup water (adjust as needed) to make a saucy consistency.
	•	Stir well and let it cook for 1–2 minutes.
	5.	Add Momos
	•	Toss in the fried momos and coat them well with the gravy.
	6.	Finish & Serve
	•	Garnish with chopped coriander.

Aaloo Paratha 🥔🥞
.
Ingredients:

For the Dough:
	•	2 cups wheat flour
	•	Water (to knead)
	•	Salt to taste

For the Filling:
	•	3 medium boiled potatoes (mashed)
	•	1 small onion, finely chopped
	•	1-2 green chillies, finely chopped
	•	1 tbsp fresh coriander (dhaniya), chopped
	•	1 tsp sukha dhaniya powder (dry coriander)
	•	1 packet Maggi Masala
	•	1 tsp Kasuri Methi (crushed)
	•	½ tsp Garam Masala
	•	½ tsp Chaat Masala
	•	½ tsp Bhuna Jeera (roasted cumin powder)
	•	Salt to taste

For Cooking:
	•	Ghee or oil

Instructions:
	1.	Prepare Dough:
	•	Knead soft dough with flour, salt, and water. Rest for 15-20 minutes.
	2.	Make Filling:
	•	Mix mashed aloo, onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, and all spices: sukha dhaniya, Maggi masala, kasuri methi, garam masala, chaat masala, bhuna jeera, and salt.
	•	Combine well and keep aside.
	3.	Roll & Fill:
	•	Take a small dough ball, roll it out a bit, place stuffing, seal and gently roll again.
	4.	Cook:
	•	Roast on hot tawa with ghee or oil till both sides turn golden brown and crisp.

Ingredients (1 glass):
	•	8–10 fresh mint leaves
	•	½ lemon (cut into wedges)
	•	½ tsp black salt (adjust to taste)
	•	1 tbsp powdered sugar
	•	1 cup crushed ice
	•	200 ml chilled Sprite (or any lemon soda)

Method:
	1.	In a tall glass, add mint leaves, lemon wedges, black salt, and powdered sugar.
	2.	Lightly muddle them to release lemon juice & mint aroma.
	3.	Fill the glass with crushed ice.
	4.	Pour chilled Sprite over the ice.
	5.	Stir gently, garnish with mint sprig + lemon slice.

**Summary**:
- machine learning is the general term for when computers learn from data
- there are lots of different ways ("algorithms") that machines can learn 
- the algorithms can be grouped into supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement algorithms*

- the data that you feed to a machine learning algorithm can be input-output pairs or just inputs
- supervised learning algorithms require input-output pairs (i.e. they require the output)
- unsupervised learning requires only the input data (not the outputs)

- here is how, in general, supervised algorithms work:
- you feed it an example input, then the associated output
- you repeat the above step many many times
- eventually, the algorithm picks up a pattern between the inputs and outputs
- now, you can feed it a brand new input, and it will predict the output for you

- here is how, in general, unsupervised algorithms work:
- you feed it an example input (without the associated output)
- you repeat the above step many times
- eventually, the algorithm clusters your inputs into groups
- now, you can feed it a brand new input, and the algorithm will predict which cluster it belongs with

* the first example in this video used the k-nearest neighbor algorithm, which is a supervised machine learning algorithm

Hope that was useful to someone!

1. Starting a Business: It's not necessary to start with a creative idea; what matters is finding something you're passionate about and can execute well. Starting a business isn't just about filling a market gap but about applying a business mindset to what you love.

2. Key to Success: Patience and the ability to delay personal gratification to build a solid foundation are crucial. Building relationships with customers, creating value, and focusing on company culture are also key factors.

3. Finding a Partner: A co-founder can bring significant value if they have complementary skills and share your business goals and ethics.

4. Learning to Fail: Failure is an integral part of the success process. Accepting and learning from failures helps build resilience and the ability to bounce back.

5. Marketing and PR Strategy: Marketing is not just about promoting a product but also about connecting with customers and building a brand. PR should be strategic and targeted.

6. Attracting Investors: It's important to know what you need from an investor and find ways to attract them based on the value you can offer, not just the capital.

Key points about how bomb size affects fallout: Larger fireball: A larger bomb creates a bigger fireball which draws in more debris from the surrounding environment, increasing the amount of material that becomes radioactive and can be dispersed as fallout. Higher altitude reach: A bigger explosion propels radioactive particles to higher altitudes, allowing them to travel further with prevailing winds before settling as fallout. Increased particle size variation: Larger bombs can produce a wider range of particle sizes in the fallout cloud, with some particles remaining airborne for longer periods, further extending the potential fallout zone. Factors influencing fallout beyond bomb size: Detonation height: Exploding a bomb at a higher altitude can minimize local fallout but potentially spread radioactive material over a larger area due to wind patterns. comment_text:
One key factor in self-motivation is the belief in one's own abilities, also known as self-efficacy. People who have high self-efficacy tend to be more motivated to achieve their goals, as they have confidence in their ability to succeed. In contrast, those with low self-efficacy may be less likely to pursue challenging goals, as they believe they lack the necessary skills or resources.

Another important factor is the value we place on our goals. When we perceive a goal as being personally meaningful or important, we are more likely to be motivated to pursue it. In contrast, goals that are seen as irrelevant or unimportant may not elicit the same level of motivation.

The environment in which we work or study also plays a role in self-motivation. People are more likely to be motivated when they feel supported and valued by others, such as peers, mentors, or supervisors. On the other hand, a negative or unsupportive environment can undermine motivation and lead to burnout.

Finally, intrinsic motivation - the drive to engage in an activity for its own sake, rather than for external rewards or pressures - is a powerful force in self-motivation. When we are intrinsically motivated, we are more likely to persist in our efforts and feel a sense of enjoyment and satisfaction in the process.

I combine my current knowledge with the content from this speech to create a blueprint for intrinsic motivation. Please give it a read:
In order for one to be self-motivated, one needs to be equipped with a sense of:

1. Competent: 
  - What: Being empowered
  - Why: You are motivated to do worthwhile work what you are competent of. 
  - How: Ask yourself 3 questions: > Can I do it? (If no, break it down step by step)
                                                            > Does it work/solve the problem? (If no, what changes/implementations/updates should/must be made)
                                                            > Is it worth it? (If no, reflect upon your choices and consequences of your choices in part 2 and 3)

2. Choice
  - What: Being in autonomy
  - Why: A sense of choice in your work in order to make it an intrinsic motivation.
  - How: Make decision based on positive consequences and be mindful to consider your choices very thoroughly

3. Consequences: 
  - What:  Looking forward to the outcome of the actions
  - Why: Not feeling controlled by consequences in order to be in autonomy 
  - How: > Combine it with making choices, consider carefully if your choices are based on a positive or negative consequences.
              > Being aware that autonomy comes from wanting positive outcomes, while control comes from avoiding negative outcomes.
              > Make a choice to seek success (positive consequences) instead of to avoid failures/punishments (negative consequences).
              > Sit back and reflect mindfully about the choices you have, being mindful about the consequence of your choices.

4. Community
  - What: Seek interdepend and not independent nor codependent.
  - How: > Understand a truthfully reflect on the value of oneself, while recognising your weaknesses
              > Recognise what, when, and where you may need help by others.
              > Learn to be patient and effective in communicating with others.
              > Build a healthy self-esteem, being mindful about ego.
              > Taking and accepting feedback mindfully, seeing feedback as a chance to improve competency (1) and not a negative criticism (3).

I've struggled with starting and keep doing something for a long time. But I found out that motivation is a myth  that we keep telling ourselves we need in order to mask actual feelings and thoughts. You need:
1) A goal u want to achieve, anything can be a goal (ex: 2h of study per day), but the catch is that u must say if u can have exceptions to the rule or not. This will come in handy later, when u will have tricky thoughts like "I had a hard day and I deserve to finish early today because... (rationalization)".
2) A way to measure time because otherwise u will never have a start and an end. A schedule will do or my way is that I set a timer 25min before I do a task and then pomodoro 6/50 with 10 min breaks. Usually I take 25 min after 3 hours. Now u don't have to do this much and actually u shouldn't.
3) If u feel like a panic attack is coming when u think about having to sit down and start something it's most likely because the amygdala is making your body release too much cortisol in your body. I suggest u take some ashwagandha to lower it a bit.
4) There is a reason why mindfulness meditation works and it is because it teaches u to focus on your breath when thoughts surface out. I'm not sure if In my opinion it's really hard to make the difference between conscious thinking and pilot mode. Now the way u want to use this is by focusing on whatever else u can except your thoughts, especially when u have to go and do work. What I mean is focus on a sound or a picture, the wall, a chair, really anything but your thoughts. A lot of the pain comes from the dread that our mind tries to make us believe.
5) EXTRA: If u focus on your mind and try to see what the next thought that is going to come up is, u will see that none will surface.


This took me a long time to realize, and now I CAN do +6h/6day/week.

comment_text: It’s crazy how many businesses still treat social media like a place to just “post and hope.” The ones that actually see results are the ones that understand it’s basically modern storytelling. People don’t follow brands anymore, they follow personalities, angles, and vibes. If your content doesn’t feel like something a real human would stop and watch, it’s game over before you even begin. What really makes social media work now is consistency paired with positioning. You can have the best product ever, but if your content doesn’t show people why it matters in a way that feels natural, nobody cares. A lot of smaller brands I know keep momentum by repurposing clips across multiple platforms and automating some of that posting with tools like Lyftgram so they don’t burn out trying to be active everywhere. Staying visible is half the battle. Marketing today is more about presence than perfection. If you can show up often, speak directly to the people who actually want what you offer, and stay top of mind, the growth starts to snowball. Social media rewards the ones who play the long game.
